_about: Who the town's people are, beyond their trade (decision 393; the npc tree's). type_weights: each hidden personality type's share per 100 residents at the founding roll (Townsfolk.roll_type, by worker id); the types are lore's roles.json, only those agreed are rolled, and the rest are steady. The numbers are npc's drafts until Jeff weighs them. thief: the side-doing of a thief (Townsfolk.tick on the world tick): every so many steps (a day is 54000), with this chance, one of the first of takes the store holds more than leave of goes missing (a ledger line by 'missing', no name; never the last of anything). Decision 461 (Jeff: 'thieves could be the answer to balancing the economy'): first gold_take gold from the richest purse above economy's folk.rich_above (never the poor, the dole, a resting companion or the coffer; Production.lift_gold), the store only when nobody is rich; store goods go back through the town's merchant (Economy.fence: the store pays raw price x fence, the merchant keeps margin of it, the thief the rest); the victim at the same meeting place is drawn against caught, a guard there (or at work for the store) against caught_guard: the gold goes back, the catch is on the cards and a dispute in the town's log; caught caught_before_lying_low times within caught_season_days days he lies low lie_low_days days.

runner._: Decision 546, npc's side: Pip, the priest's apprentice, carries the temple's alms (economy's altar_gold) down to the barrow's altar once a day from hour, hours_each_way each way, on the world tick whether or not anyone is near; while away he is off the streets. Once any player has learned Aldous's secret, a run goes wrong with lost_chance: he stays lost below (the gold with him, not down) until a player comes within found_reach of the barrow's niche place. His card: the companion table's look (CompanionCard legacy) and these leanings, not a roll. Amended 2026-10-20: the town's own resident of his name becomes the acolyte in place, his trades this trade alone (Production.retrain), his bench left for the town to fill; the minted runner takes the same trade word, one no workshop asks for and not economy's apprentice system's.
runner.name: Pip

healer._: Decision 502, npc's side (amended): the medicine man gathers herbs_a_day herbs a day within six cells, by his body on his way while a player is near, else around his hut's cell once gather_hour has come; delivered to the town's store at the delivery price.

sick._: Decision 501: sickness. Each day, by town, every resident not away and not sick (a companion resting there too) has chance of falling sick, times winter in winter, times hungry after a hungry or doled day, times old for the old; at most one new case a town a day. They keep to their bed; treated (the medicine man's visit of visit_hours, a walk to the healer's hut, a remedy in hand) it ends the next morning; untreated it ends after days, and then one of the town's own who is old dies with death_old (never a rescued captive or a settled arrival this step, the coordinator's guard). kinds: the words.

scoundrel._: Decision 492: the scoundrel's side-doing. short: the chance a thing he makes that is measured by count or weight (Items.measured; never gear) comes out short, at weight of its full (ItemBook.make_short, items'); his debt he never pays back on his own (economy's repay by type), and when it first reaches the bank's cap the town's official learns it, his card too, and with rulings on it is a dispute before the lawspeaker.

strays._: Decision 487: now and then (every steps, with chance, one at a time per town) one of a town's people of these trades loses their way beyond the walls: away (no work, no meals) at a far cell of the town's own zone (at least far cells from the store, off held ground, reachable by the routes), their body there while a player is near; walked home by a player (the arrival pays commissions.escort) or back on their own after days. Never an official (origin appointed), the merchant, or an outcast.

hail._lively: 554 amended, a trial on Jeff's word (2026-10-22): the hail's user turn allows one small everyday detail within the bound (no person, place, name, price or contradiction invented); false turns the strict sentence back on.
hail._note: Residents speaking unprompted (decision 554, narrowing 336): a resident with something to say (Resident.hail_cue: a plea of their own, what the town noted today, a ruling of the lawspeaker today, the sky turning, a greeting by standing) says one line as a player first comes within talking reach that day, the lowest ask of all. on: the switch; quiet_seconds: no hail to a player who gave or took a blow this recently; minute_seconds: one hail in a player's hearing per this long, and none within it of a resident's answer to them; slow_ticks: no hails while the resident mind's last answer took longer; said_kept: how many said cues a card keeps, so the same thing is not said twice; greetings_a_day: greetings by standing a player hears in a day from the whole town (the first residents met), so a newcomer is greeted, not mobbed (the coordinator, after the soak).

_asleep: Decision 751: the line a player gets for clicking a townsman asleep in bed, picked by the body's id; %s the name, else "The <trade>". Voice's words (2026-10-31).
_balance: Decision 761, npc's side (2): the balance quest's herder. hail, once a day to a player near while his fold's quest is open; ask on a click (grudge in its place to one who has left meat lying); flock_some ({had}, {left} as words) or flock_half (half or more gone); days ({days} as "two days") or days_last; the ending (balanced, off, badly) once to each after the judgement; party, by ending, to the players in the area (%s his name). Voice's words (2026-11-01).

hail: You there. The wolves are at my sheep.
Wolves on the hill again, and my sheep with them.
Mind yourself up there; the wolves are at my fold.
ask: Wolves are taking my sheep, and it's the deer that draw them. Thin the deer, and carry the meat down to the town's store. Leave it lying and you'll only bring more wolves.
The deer bring the wolves, and the wolves take my sheep. Put a few deer down and bring the meat home to the store; meat left on the hill feeds them.
Too many deer on the hill, so too many wolves. Bring some down, and take the meat to the town's store. Don't leave it lying; they come for that too.
flock_half: Half my flock's gone, and more.
Most of my sheep are gone.
There's hardly a flock left to count.
days: The flock will hold {days} more, no longer.
In {days} I'll know how it's gone.
You've {days} more before they've had the lot.
days_last: This is the last day. By tomorrow we'll know.
It ends tonight, one way or the other.
Last day. Whatever's done, it's done by dark.
grudge: You left a carcass to rot on my hill. The wolves thank you for it.
That deer you left lying? The wolves found it, and then my sheep.
You put a deer down and left it there. That's more wolves at my fold.
balanced_few: Few left, but the wolves have gone. We'll build it back.
A pair's enough to start again, now the wolves have drawn off.
Not much of a flock, but it's safe now. It'll grow back, a lamb at a time.
balanced: The flock holds. There'll be lambs soon. Thank you.
Fewer wolves, and the sheep have settled. Lambs coming, too.
You kept it right. The flock's whole, and lambing.
off: It didn't hold. The flock's gone; give me a few days.
Not a sheep left. It'll be a few days before I've a flock again.
Gone, all of them. I'll start again in a few days.
badly: The flock's gone, and the wolves won't stop at my fold. Bar your doors tonight.
They've had every sheep. Now they'll come down to the town after dark.
All gone. The wolves are fat and bold now, and the town is next.

party.balanced: %s's flock holds; the wolves have drawn off.
party.badly: %s's flock is lost to the wolves, and they are coming to the town by night.

_threat: Decision 762: threat in town. refused, narrated to a player whose Barter or trade a sheltering one refuses (%s the name); sheltering, spoken when clicked while sheltering; all_clear, spoken by the first out when it lifts. By kind, wolves or raid. Voice's words (2026-11-01).

wolves: %s will not open up with wolves in the lanes.
%s keeps the door shut while wolves are in the lanes.
%s stays behind a barred door until the wolves are gone.
raid: %s will not open up with raiders in the town.
%s keeps the door barred while raiders are in the town.
%s stays behind a barred door until the raiders are gone.

wolves: Wolves in the lanes. Come back when they're gone.
Not now; there are wolves about.
raid: Raiders about. Not now, not with them out there.
Keep your voice down; there are raiders in the town.
Not now. Come back when the raiders have gone.

wolves: The wolves have gone. Back to work.
No more wolves. Out you come.
raid: The raiders have gone. Open the shutters.
They're gone. Out you come, all of you.

_healer_left: Decision 759: a healer leaving his hut in old age; heard, the fact the nearest town's people learn; told, the line to a player in the hut's care. %s the name. Voice's words (2026-11-01), lore's fine.

healer_left.heard: %s the healer has left the hut in the wilds for good, too old now to live so far from town.
healer_left.told: %s has left the healer's hut for good. It stands empty, but while it stands you will still wake there.

greet._note: A click on a townsperson (decision 560, npc's side; Jeff: they stop, turn and address you). stop_seconds: how long they stand facing the player; again_seconds: one greeting a pair in this long (a click within it only turns them again); refuse: the word when they cannot stop (in bed, hiding, strayed, escorting, an ask of theirs out); standing: the word for one the town knows (Standing.words: wronged, known, trusted; a stranger gets the trade's); trades: a trade's lines, one picked a day (the default's for a trade not listed). The word is said at once without the mind; what they have to tell the player today follows as a hail (554) under its limits.
greet.care: You're in my care; fall where you will, I'll see to you.

medicine_man: Herbs, if you have any; the town is short of them.
Sit; let me look at you.
smith: What is it? The forge won't wait.
Aye? Make it quick, the iron's hot.
cook: What is it? The pot's on.
priest: Peace on you. What is it?
hunter: Quiet, you'll scare the game. What?
butcher: Wipe your feet, there's blood about.
farmer: What is it? The field won't hoe itself.
hauler: What? I've a load to shift.
herder: Up from the hills with the drove. What is it?
The weather holds, for now. What?

visitors._about: npc's side of visitors (decision 711, npc's side): what a stranger passing through says when clicked. greetings by kind (traveller, pedlar, pilgrim), %s where they come from; road: their news when the towns have none to carry, %s again where they come from; leaving: said once they are on their way out. Each player gets one piece of their news a visit.

vendor: Blades for the road, one gold apiece. Take your pick.
Starting out? A gold buys you something to swing.
One gold each, and never sold dear. What'll it be?
traveller: Long road from %s. Is the inn any good?
pedlar: Fine things from %s, if you've the coin.
Come and look. All the way from %s.
pilgrim: Peace on you. I've walked from %s to pray here.
The gods keep you. I came from %s.

road: The road from %s was quiet, thank the gods.
Nothing much stirring on the road from %s.
leaving: I'm on my way. Fare you well.
Off down the road. Gods keep you.
